quick_connect.title: Wireless from a Windows laptop
steps: Switch the screen on with the black Sharp remote (blue POWER ON button), or wait – it wakes when it sees you.
On your laptop press Win + K to open the Cast panel (Wi-Fi needs to be switched on, but you do not need to be joined to any network).
Choose "EDR1-AirMedia" from the list, then type the 4-digit code shown on the screen when asked for the PIN, and press Connect.

quick_connect.title: Wired with the USB-C cable on the table
steps: Plug the USB-C cable from the black table box into your laptop's USB-C port.
Your screen appears automatically.
In Teams or Zoom, the camera, microphone and speakers switch to "Yealink" by themselves – use this route for any online call.
quick_connect.recommended_for: Macs, iPads, and any Teams / Zoom / hybrid meeting

quick_connect.title: Mac or iPad
steps: Use the USB-C cable on the table – Apple Screen Mirroring does not reach this screen.
Your display appears automatically; no code needed.

howto.title: Running a Teams or Zoom meeting
steps: Connect by the USB-C cable (not wireless) so the room camera and mics are used.
Start your meeting on your laptop as normal.
Check the device settings in the call: camera, microphone and speaker should all say Yealink.
Point the silver Yealink remote at the bar to adjust the call volume.

howto.title: Nothing on the screen?
steps: Is the screen on? Press the blue POWER ON button on the black Sharp remote.
Wireless: press Win + K again and reconnect. Wi-Fi on your laptop must be on; a phone hotspot is fine, it is not the network that matters.
Wired: unplug the USB-C cable and plug it back in; try the other USB-C port on your laptop.
Still nothing: use the Help button at the top of this page.

howto.title: No sound, or sound from the laptop instead of the room
steps: Click the speaker icon on your laptop and choose Yealink as the output.
For calls, volume is on the silver Yealink remote; for presentation sound it is on the black Sharp remote.
Wireless connections send audio too, but the wired cable is more reliable for sound.

howto.title: Leaving the room
steps: Unplug the USB-C cable and leave it on the table.
Stop sharing (Win + K → Disconnect) so the next person does not see your desktop.
The screen switches itself off; no need to power anything down.
